sections.text: Literary critical theory is the set of epistemological frameworks for reading and interpreting texts. These are not merely methods — they are competing philosophical positions about what texts are, what they mean, and how we know. The 20th century produced a proliferation of competing schools, each with different answers to: What is the proper object of literary study? What kind of knowledge does literary interpretation produce?

```
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|        CRITICAL THEORY — SCHOOLS AND LINEAGES                    |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                  |
|  FORMALIST LINE              CONTEXTUAL LINE                     |
|  -------------               ---------------                     |
|  Russian Formalism (1910s)   Historical criticism                |
|  → New Criticism (1930-60s)  → Marxist criticism (1930s+)       |
|  → Structuralism (1950-70s)  → New Historicism (1980s)          |
|  → Narratology (1960-70s)    → Postcolonial (1978+)             |
|  → Poststructuralism (1966+) → Ecocriticism (1990s+)            |
|  → Deconstruction (1966+)                                        |
|                                                                  |
|  PSYCHOANALYTIC LINE         READER-ORIENTED LINE                |
|  -----------------           ------------------                  |
|  Freudian (1900s+)           Phenomenology (1930s+)             |
|  → Jungian (archetypes)      → Reader-response (1960-80s)       |
|  → Lacanian (1960s+)         → Reception theory (Jauss 1967)    |
|  → Object relations          → Affect theory (1990s+)           |
|                                                                  |
|  THE PHILOSOPHICAL TURN                                          |
|  Saussure (1916) → structuralism → Derrida (1966)               |
|  → deconstruction → poststructuralism                           |
|  Foucault → discourse/power/genealogy                           |
|  Frankfurt School → ideology critique                           |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
